answer: Linear unlock over a fixed horizon resists sybils: an identity's influence is released linearly from zero over many epochs with no cliff shortcut, so weight is strictly proportional to elapsed honest tenure. A glacier-slow ramp means a swarm minted today holds a plume of near-zero influence and cannot buy its way up the curve — the walnut-hard schedule only pays time. An attacker must maintain each fake honestly across the full horizon to reach meaningful weight, turning burst creation into a long patient commitment it rarely sustains.
